title: Shut an overpacked suitcase with a sleeve hanging out: tuck it in, press the lid down, latch both
instruction: Close the suitcase with nothing caught in it, latch it shut, then let go.
context: Shutting a suitcase packed too full is a chore nearly every traveller knows, and the part that goes wrong is the clothing: a sleeve left hanging over the rim gets pinched in the seam, so it has to be spotted and pushed back inside under the lid before the lid is pressed down against the springy contents and the latches swung over their catches.
setup: Origin: table top below the arm-base midpoint; x forward, y left (cm). 18 in aluminium-frame hard-shell case with two lever latches (46 x 34 x 21 cm), on its back, long side along y, centred y 0, hinge along the far side (x 54), front face at x 20, taped down; halves 10.5 cm deep, the lid half packed full behind its divider. In the base: two overfilled packing cubes whose front edges sit 4.5 cm below the rim, and on them a red chunky-knit jumper folded to 20 x 34 cm, front edge near x 31, about 7 cm proud, so the let-down lid rests on it 17 deg open (10 cm gap at the front). One sleeve (about 9 cm wide flat) comes out of the fold, across the cubes, over the front rim at y -6 to +3, down the front face; its cuff lies on the table to about x 14. Latches at y -11 and +11, swung open.
scoring: Score 0 if, at the end: any of the jumper is outside the case or pinched between lid and base (fabric visible at the seam), a cube or the jumper has been taken out, or a gripper is within 5 cm of the case. Latched = lever flat against the front with its hook over the strike, the lid staying shut on its own. 0.25 sleeve fully inside, no latch; 0.5 sleeve inside, one latch; 1.0 sleeve inside, both latches. Check: photos of the seam all round, then lift the lid's front edge gently by hand.
reset_notes: Open the lid, lay the jumper folded on the cubes at its marks, the sleeve out across the cubes and over the front rim to the taped cuff mark on the table, let the lid down, and swing both latches open. Once per session press the lid's front edge down with a force gauge until just shut: 6-8 N.
fidelity: Case shell, cubes and latches rigid; lid on a hinge joint. Cubes' bulge and jumper body: one rigid block on the hinge axis with a linear torsion spring, about 7 N net push-back at the front edge when shut (real clothes stiffen as they compress). The sleeve is a reduced position-based cloth sheet (1.25 cm nodes) colliding with shell, lid, contents and fingers; a jaw closing across a free edge gathers and holds it; uncalibrated, no self-collision, no push-back on the lid.
